regressions.finding: A mip smaller than its dimensions require was accepted, so consumers read past the buffer.
mipLevels=0xFFFFFFFF sized a 16 GiB mip-size table allocation from a 21-byte file.
One mip declaring 0xFFFFFFF0 bytes allocated about 4 GiB before the short file was detected.
A deflate entry declaring zero output bytes made ReadFile hand miniz a null destination (UBSan).
ReadTOC allocated the header's tocRawSize (up to 256 MB) from a TOC stream of any size.
A key that began with a UTF-8 BOM mid-document was accepted, but SaveToString emitted it as the first line and the reload stripped the BOM and rejected the empty key.

A save whose sceneName held a CR was read and listed, but the writer refuses the field, so every Load failed in DeserializeWorld without trying the .bak and the next Save rotated the unloadable primary over it; the reader now accepts only metadata the writer can re-render.

A base64 data URI declaring a 300 MB byteLength made cgltf_load_buffers allocate the declared size (up to 1 GiB) from a 373-byte file before decoding; ValidateDocumentStructure now rejects a byteLength the payload cannot fill.

A uint16 index accessor at an odd buffer-view byteOffset made cgltf_validate read indices through a misaligned typed pointer (UBSan); ValidateAccessorBounds now requires view offset, accessor offset and stride to be multiples of the component size.

A GLB whose JSON chunk length is not a multiple of 4 placed the in-place BIN buffer at an odd address, so every typed accessor read was misaligned (UBSan); ValidateDocumentStructure now rejects an unaligned BIN chunk.

A static mesh without NORMAL whose finite positions reach ~1e29 overflowed the float cross products in GenerateNormals, so LoadGLTFStaticMesh published NaN normals; the normals are now accumulated and normalized in double.
EXRLoader passed an error out-parameter to ParseEXRHeaderFromMemory, which overwrites its first strdup'd message when a second header check also fails, so every such file leaked it.

Texture::CreateFromFile returned S_OK for a file stb_image could not decode and marked it loaded with a size estimated from the requested description, so TextureSystem cached a texture that held no pixels.
tinyobjloader's default material reader joined any mtllib name onto the OBJ's directory, so a ../ name read a file outside the asset tree (and ../../dev/zero an unbounded device).
Every polygon was ear-clipped in O(n^2): one 3000-corner star in a 49 KiB file took over 4 s under ASan, and larger files grew without bound. Polygons over 96 corners are now fanned.
Normals were normalized in float: a finite authored component such as 1e20 squared to infinity and gave a zero normal, and large positions gave NaN face normals.
An EntitySpawn whose position was NaN decoded successfully and seeded a remote player's current and target position; the decoder now rejects non-finite positions.
A dynamic adjacency entry naming a triangle past the triangle array was accepted and the mesh registered.
A triangle naming a vertex past the vertex array was accepted and the mesh registered.
An 8x2 heightmap was accepted and published as resolution 8, so the clipmap indexed 64 samples of a 16-sample heightmap.

A GetAssetRequest missing its platform byte was rejected only after the decoded path had been written into the caller's struct; the path, invalidate and stats decoders shared the partial-publish pattern.
RecvFrame resized the payload to the header's claimed size before any payload byte arrived, so an 8-byte header from any local peer forced a 16 MiB allocation per frame.

DecodeSnapshot reserved up to 65,536 peers, locks or edits from the wire count before checking the bytes existed, so a 20-byte snapshot reserved several MiB; process status and argument lists were sized the same way.
The CSV loader accepted a document larger than the new 8 MiB production limit without bounding its read and parse work.
The JSON loader accepted a valid prefix followed by malformed trailing bytes and published partial table data.
A numeric-looking JSON string such as 001 was inferred as an integer and serialized as an invalid bare JSON number.
SaveToCSV wrote a single-column row with an empty cell as a blank line, which LoadFromCSV skips, so the row was lost on reload.
SaveToCSV wrote a last-column cell ending in CR unquoted, and LoadFromCSV stripped that CR as a line ending on reload.
A truncated collaboration frame changed the caller's type and peer before the decoder rejected its incomplete node ID.
The localization loader published an earlier entry from a malformed catalog instead of preserving the previous table.
The dialogue loader read and parsed a document larger than the new 8 MiB production limit without a file-size bound.
A dialogue document whose nodes field is not an array replaced the loaded tree's ID and start node before the loader rejected it.
The FPS player-state decoder accepted unknown action bits in a peer-supplied snapshot record.
The FPS player-state decoder coerced a noncanonical boolean wire byte instead of rejecting the record.
An invalid boolean wire byte decoded to a default state whose zero sequence matched batch zero, so a malformed snapshot was accepted.

The schema field was read with std::atoi over any run of digits; atoi of 4294967297 is undefined and LP64 glibc returned 1, so the reader accepted the file as schema 1. The reader now parses the integer with std::from_chars, range-checked.

String fields ended at the first quote and were never unescaped, so a ref holding an escaped quote read back as its prefix up to the backslash. The reader now unescapes exactly the escapes Save writes and refuses any other.
Backslashes were not unescaped, so every Windows destination and a generator holding a backslash read back doubled and changed on each Save and Load round trip.

A mod id had no policy beyond non-empty, so an id holding a control byte (or NUL, a path separator or 64 KiB) was published as the map key, log argument, config field and UI label. Ids are now 1-128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._-], not '.' or '..'.

Two mod directories declaring one id were both counted but only the one the directory iterator reached last was registered, so a dropped-in mod could shadow an installed one. An id claimed twice is now published from neither directory.
LoadFromFile accepted a NaN duration, so UpdatePlayback never reached the end, and a negative one broke the std::clamp precondition in SeekTo and the kill cam.
LoadFromFile accepted descending frame timestamps, breaking the sorted-range precondition of the std::lower_bound in FindFrameIndex so playback jumped backwards.
LoadFromFile read the version field and never checked it, decoding any future or corrupt layout as version 1.
The streaming .sanim loader resized a track to its declared key count before reading any key, so a 60-byte file forced a 20 MB allocation before truncation was detected.
The .sanim loader accepted a NaN clip duration, which playback feeds to fmod and divides by.
The .sanim loader accepted decreasing key times, which the key search assumes are sorted ascending.
LoadOrchestrationJournal accepted two committed mutations for one client instance, which the service's keyed replay table silently collapsed to whichever came last.
LoadOrchestrationJournal accepted two snapshot records for one process id; the writer serializes a keyed map and cannot produce that.
LoadOrchestrationJournal accepted a committed mutation with an empty client instance, a key ReadMutationKey refuses everywhere else.
LoadOrchestrationJournal accepted an INT64_MIN crash timestamp, and OrchestrationService's conversion to a system_clock time point overflowed (signed-overflow UB).
LoadOrchestrationJournal accepted an INT64_MAX drain deadline, which overflows the same system_clock conversion when a draining process is reconciled.
SQLiteConnection::Open accepted a legacy store whose escaped rewrite exceeds the store budget, so every later SET, DELETE and commit failed to publish.
SQLiteConnection::Open accepted an escaped-format store whose raw tabs double when rewritten, past the store budget, leaving the store unwritable.
The character row reader accepted rows with more than 15 fields and silently ignored the extra ones.
BuildCharacterSave wrote positions and stats with iostream's 6 significant digits, so a load-save cycle moved the character and changed its stats.
std::stoul accepted -1 for the account id and wrapped it to 4294967295.
std::stof accepted nan for a position, so a NaN location reached gameplay on login.
std::stoi stopped at the first non-digit, so a level of 12abc loaded as 12.
std::istream negated -1 into the unsigned epoch, loading UINT64_MAX so no later Prepare could ever advance that session's fence.
The epoch state reader accepted a leading plus sign on an area id.
std::istream wrapped -4294967295 to phase 1, restoring a Prepare fence the file never recorded.
ParseSparkMatDefinition accepted nan/inf factors (std::stof), which RegisterMaterial's std::clamp passes through to the GPU constant buffers; non-finite factors now keep their value.
LocalFileProvider::ReadFile opened the mount root directory on Linux and sized its buffer from the INT64_MAX ext4 directory end offset, aborting the process; only regular files are read now.
A virtual path naming a mounted subdirectory reached the same INT64_MAX allocation in LocalFileProvider::ReadFile on ext4; directories now read as nothing.
A brace inside a quoted recent-project name truncated the hand-rolled field scan; the reader now retains the field boundary.
A bracket inside a quoted scene path disrupted the project-field scan; the reader now retains the complete path.
An oversized project timestamp could throw during numeric conversion; the reader now rejects it.
An INI scene transform could import non-finite coordinates; the reader now rejects them.
A theme colour could import non-finite components; the reader now rejects them.
A window monitor index outside int32 range could narrow with undefined behavior; the reader now rejects it.
An overflowing dock coordinate could throw or become non-finite; the reader now rejects it.
An overflowing layout size could throw or become non-finite; the reader now rejects it.
An overflowing tab order could narrow outside its integer range; the reader now rejects it.
